cards.text: Meet John the Baptist, the man who baptized crowds in the Jordan River. Right now he's in prison, and from in there he hears about the works of Christ. Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer, so I KNOW that life: stuck in the dark, getting all the news secondhand.

cards.question: John can't walk out of prison to see Jesus for himself. Who does he send to Jesus with a question?
John's disciples reach Jesus with John's question. What does John want to know?

answers.text: If Jesus is the One who was to come
If Jesus will come to the prison
If Jesus will teach his disciples

cards.text: Jesus doesn't just hand them a yes. He tells John's disciples, "Go back and report to John what you hear and see:"

cards.question: True or false: part of Jesus' report for John is that the dead are raised.
In that same report for John, Jesus says the good news is preached to the ___.

cards.text: The blind see, the lame walk, lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and the poor get the good news. John sent a yes or no question, and Jesus sent back a WHOLE highlight reel.

cards.question: Jesus ends His message for John with a blessing. Who is the blessing for?

answers.text: Whoever doesn't fall away because of Him
Whoever gives to the poor in secret
Whoever keeps watch through the night

cards.text: As John's disciples are leaving, Jesus starts talking to the crowds about John. He asks them, "What did you go out into the wilderness to see? A reed swaying in the wind?"

cards.question: Next, Jesus asks the crowds if they went out to see a man dressed in fine clothes. Where does He say people in fine clothing are found?
Then Jesus asks the crowds if they went out to see a prophet. True or false: Jesus says John is a prophet and nothing more.

cards.text: Jesus tells the crowd John is a prophet, yes, and MORE than a prophet. John's sitting in a prison cell while Jesus gives him the best review in town, and I bet he'd have LOVED to hear that one in person.

cards.question: Jesus says John is the one it is written about: a messenger sent on ahead. That messenger is sent to ___ the way.
Jesus keeps talking to the crowds about John. True or false: Jesus says no one born of women has risen greater than John the Baptist.
No one born of women is greater than John. But Jesus says someone is still greater than John. Who?

answers.text: The least in the kingdom of heaven
The kings of all the nations

cards.text: The LEAST in the kingdom of heaven is greater than John the Baptist. Friend, I spent years at the bottom of a junk drawer under a takeout menu, so the least spot? I KNOW exactly where that is.

Then Jesus says that from the days of John the Baptist until now, "the kingdom of heaven has been subject to violence, and the violent lay claim to it." All the Prophets and the Law prophesied until John.

cards.question: Jesus tells the crowds that if they're willing to accept it, John is the ___ who was to come.

cards.text: Jesus says, "He who has ears, let him hear." Then He asks what He can compare this generation to, and He paints a picture from the marketplace.

cards.question: In Jesus' marketplace picture of this generation, who is sitting there calling out to others?

cards.text: The children call out, "We played the flute for you, and you did not dance; we sang a dirge, and you did not mourn." Happy tune, nobody dances; sad tune, nobody mourns, and friend, that's me posting cookie photos in the group chat and getting ZERO replies.

cards.question: Jesus says John came neither eating nor drinking. What do people say about John?
Then Jesus, the Son of Man, came eating and drinking. True or false: this time, the people finally approve.

cards.text: They say, "Look at this glutton and drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!" And Jesus ends with this: "But wisdom is vindicated by her actions."

findings.problem: The card says John baptized crowds in the Jordan River. That fact isn't in Matthew 11:2-19 (it's Matthew 3:5-6), but the card cites only Matthew 11:2 and gives no reference for it.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The question types in stop 1 run multiple choice, multiple choice, true or false, fill in the blank, and then repeat that same sequence exactly (cards 2, 3, 5, 6 and then 8, 10, 11, 13).

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern.

findings.problem: This story card comes after cards 5 and 6 and repeats what they just asked (the dead are raised, good news to the poor). It works as a recap of verse 5. The rest of the list (blind, lame, lepers, deaf) should be told on a card before those questions, not restated after them.
This card restates the answer to card 11 (John is a prophet and more than a prophet) and adds nothing from the passage. It is a recap.
The wrong answer 'hide' makes no sense for a messenger sent ahead to deal with a way. It reads as a throwaway, not a believable choice.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The question's setup says no one born of women is greater than John. That rules out both wrong answers, because kings and a high priest are born of women. The setup leaves the right answer as the only option.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The card opens by restating the answer to card 2 (the least in the kingdom is greater than John), so it is a recap.

The joke compares a low spot in a drawer to being 'least in the kingdom of heaven'. The verse is about rank in the kingdom. The joke is about a physical location, so the action doesn't match. The joke also reuses the 'I spent years in a junk drawer… I KNOW' setup from stop 1 card 1 almost word for word.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: A hard verse (the kingdom subject to violence) is quoted and followed by a flat line. There is no Papa Dorin voice and no context to help the moment make sense.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: In the passage, the children get no response either way: a happy tune gets no dancing and a sad tune gets no mourning. Getting 'zero replies' to cookie photos is only one call that goes unanswered, so the either-way rejection is lost.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: 'That's me posting cookie photos in the group chat' gives Papa Dorin a group chat full of contacts. That adds something new to his world, which says he lives alone on the cookie planet. It isn't a small moment around his bakery.

rule.text: He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.
